Goal: one “sale page system” that lets you spin up robust, Square-powered pages at localeffortfood.com/[sale-slug] in minutes—no new repo per sale unless you want it.

TL;DR design

One dynamic route: /[sale] renders any sale from Sanity by slug. Two layout variants (“Standard” ≈ your SalePage, “Paikka” ≈ your PaikkaPage) chosen in content.

Sanity = the builder: you (or a tiny internal UI) create a Sale doc, attach Products, pick layout/theme, pickup window, email template, tracking, etc.

Square first, 3 levels
A. Checkout Links (fastest, safest) — per product, no cart.
B. Inline Checkout (Web Payments SDK) — simple cart; serverless Order+Payment.
C. Subscriptions / inventory — opt-in with Square APIs.

Webhooks mirror: Square → webhook → Supabase table for “orders” & live counts; update page tracker—no Firestore.

ISR + webhooks: on any Sanity change or order, revalidate the page.

Optional microfrontend: if main app deploys are flaky, you can auto-scaffold apps/sale-[slug] from a template and proxy /[slug] to it.

(You referenced these two pages; we’ll unify their good parts under one renderer: PaikkaPage.jsx and SalePage.jsx.)

Minimal schema (Sanity)

sale (document)

slug (required), title, layout (“standard” | “paikka”), hero, tagline

window: start/end, timezone, pickup instructions, location

theme: colors, card style, gallery

products: array of saleProduct

tracking: metaPixelId, utmSource, gtag

email: brevoTemplateId, senderName

stats: soldCount (display cache)

square: locationId, checkoutMode (“link” | “inline”), webhookTag

product (document)

title, image, desc

priceDisplay (optional override)

squareItemId, squareVariationId, squareCheckoutLinkUrl (at least one)

inventoryMode: “square” | “manual”; manualQty (optional)

saleProduct (object)

product (ref), order, limitPerCustomer, hide, badge, priceOverride

Why: Sanity handles all editorial; Square handles money; Supabase handles live counters/history (transactional). No Firestore.

Pages & endpoints (Next.js / Vite + adapter)

src/pages/[sale].tsx → fetch sale by slug, choose layout component, render.

src/components/sale/*
SaleRenderer, SaleHero, ProductGrid, ProductCard, CheckoutButton, PickupBlock, Tracker, Faq.

API:

api/square/create-checkout (only if checkoutMode=inline)

api/square/webhook (orders/payments → upsert Supabase; bump stats.soldCount; trigger revalidate)

api/revalidate (Sanity webhook target)

Render flow

Load Sale via GROQ; if layout="paikka", apply Paikka theme; else Standard.

For each product: if squareCheckoutLinkUrl present → button is plain link; else if inline → POST to create-checkout and redirect.

Tracker queries Supabase orders view aggregated by sale slug.

Square integration choices

Tier A: Checkout Links (recommended first)

Create one link per product/variation (CLI below). Store the URLs in the product doc. No PCI complexity; ultra-robust.

Tier B: Inline checkout

Use Web Payments SDK to tokenize; your API creates an Order + Payment (or Checkout) server-side with metadata { saleSlug, productId, customerEmail }.

Keep SAQ A by never touching raw PAN; Square token only.

Webhooks

Subscribe to payment.created, payment.updated, order.updated.

On success: upsert orders(sale_slug, product_id, qty, amount, square_payment_id) in Supabase; increment cached counters; call ISR revalidate for /[sale].

Builder: two ways

Sanity Studio “Create Sale”: initial-value template that opens a guided form, fetches Square Catalog (serverless function), and patches products with square… IDs or link URLs.

CLI (packages/cli):

pnpm dlx le sale new <slug> \
  --title "Paikka Presale" \
  --layout paikka \
  --products "smoked-chicken:ITEM_ID/VAR_ID" "pumpkin-romesco:ITEM_ID/VAR_ID" \
  --window "2025-10-20/2025-10-25" \
  --pickup "Paikka, St. Paul • Fri 11–2"


Creates Sanity Sale doc

(Optionally) creates Square Checkout Links (Tier A) and patches product docs

Kicks a preview deploy or ISR ping

Hosting at /[name-of-sale]

Keep it in the main web app: add [sale].tsx and a catch-all rewrite for any reserved paths.

If you must isolate: deploy a microfrontend to Vercel/Amplify and add a reverse proxy rewrite in the main app:

/[slug] → https://sale-[slug].your-host.app/ (preserves your canonical domain).
